Question 1
?

Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation T:(u,v,w)→(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w)), given that u=2x+y,v=−x+3y−2z,w=3y+4z.

a
116
b
140
c
16
d
8
e
40
Submit

decision.explanation: The Jacobian matrix of (u,v,w) with respect to (x,y,z) is [[2,1,0],[-1,3,-2],[0,3,4]], whose determinant is 2(12+6)-(-4)=40. The requested transformation is its inverse, so its Jacobian determinant is 1/40.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation $T:(u,v,w)\to (x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w)),$ given that 

$$
u=2x+y,\,v=-x+3y-2z,\,w=3y+4z.
$$
after.worked_solution:
For a transformation 

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{aligned}],
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & \frac{∂x}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & \frac{∂y}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & \frac{∂z}{∂w}\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, we're only given ${T}^{-1}.$ So, we compute the Jacobian determinant of $T$ as follows:

- First, we compute $\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)},$ the Jacobian determinant of ${T}^{-1}.$

- Then, we will compute the Jacobian determinant of $T$ using the relation

$$
\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1}.
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & =2 & \,\frac{∂u}{∂y} & =1 & \,\frac{∂u}{∂z} & =0 \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & =-1 & \,\frac{∂v}{∂y} & =3 & \,\frac{∂v}{∂z} & =-2 \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & =0 & \,\frac{∂w}{∂y} & =3 & \,\frac{∂w}{∂z} & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant of ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} & \frac{∂u}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y} & \frac{∂v}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & \frac{∂w}{∂y} & \frac{∂w}{∂z}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 3 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =2|\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}|-1|\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =2(12+6)-1(-4-0) \\  & =40.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we take the reciprocal:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & ={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{40}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation T:(u,v,w)→(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w)), given that u=2x+y,v=−x+3y−2z,w=3y+4z.

a
116
b
140
c
16
d
8
e
40
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a transformation

T:[uvw]→[x(u,v,w)y(u,v,w)z(u,v,w)],

the Jacobian determinant of T, denoted ∂(x,y,z)∂(u,v,w), is given by

∂(x,y,z)∂(u,v,w)=|∂x∂u∂x∂v∂x∂w∂y∂u∂y∂v∂y∂w∂z∂u∂z∂v∂z∂w|.

In this case, we're only given T−1. So, we compute the Jacobian determinant of T as follows:

  • First, we compute ∂(u,v,w)∂(x,y,z), the Jacobian determinant of T−1.

  • Then, we will compute the Jacobian determinant of T using the relation ∂(x,y,z)∂(u,v,w)=(∂(u,v,w)∂(x,y,z))−1.

First, we find the partial derivatives:

∂u∂x=2∂u∂y=1∂u∂z=0∂v∂x=−1∂v∂y=3∂v∂z=−2∂w∂x=0∂w∂y=3∂w∂z=4

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant of T−1 is

∂(u,v,w)∂(x,y,z)=|∂u∂x∂u∂y∂u∂z∂v∂x∂v∂y∂v∂z∂w∂x∂w∂y∂w∂z|=|210−13−2034|=2|3−234|−1|−1−204|=2(12+6)−1(−4−0)=40.

Finally, we take the reciprocal:

∂(x,y,z)∂(u,v,w)=(∂(u,v,w)∂(x,y,z))−1=140.

before.html:
Question 2
?

Find the locations of all of the critical points of the transformation T, where T is defined as

T:[uvw]⟶[u2−vu2+vew].

a
The critical points lie on the plane w=u.
b
The critical points lie on the parabolic cylinder w2=2u.
c
The critical points lie on the sphere u2+v2+w2=1.
d
The critical points lie on the uv−plane.
e
The critical points lie on the vw−plane.
Submit

decision.explanation: The derivative matrix is [[2u,-1,0],[2u,1,0],[0,0,e^w]], with determinant 4u e^w. Critical points occur where this determinant is zero. Since e^w is always positive, this happens exactly when u=0, which is the vw-plane.

answers.correct_value: The critical points lie on the $vw-$plane.
answers.wrong_value: The critical points lie on the $uv-$plane.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Find the locations of all of the critical points of the transformation $T,$ where $T$ is defined as

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{u}^{2}-v \\ {u}^{2}+v \\ {e}^{w}\end{aligned}].
$$
after.worked_solution:
For a transformation 

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{aligned}],
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & \frac{∂x}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & \frac{∂y}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & \frac{∂z}{∂w}\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Here, we have 

$$
x(u,v,w)={u}^{2}-v,\,y(u,v,w)={u}^{2}+v,\,z(u,v,w)={e}^{w}.
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & =2u & \,\frac{∂x}{∂v} & =-1 & \,\frac{∂x}{∂w} & =0 \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & =2u & \,\frac{∂y}{∂v} & =1 & \,\frac{∂y}{∂w} & =0 \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & =0 & \,\frac{∂z}{∂v} & =0 & \,\frac{∂z}{∂w} & ={e}^{w}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =|\begin{aligned}2u & -1 & 0 \\ 2u & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {e}^{w}\end{aligned}| \\  & ={e}^{w}|\begin{aligned}2u & -1 \\ 2u & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & ={e}^{w}(2u+2u) \\  & =4u{e}^{w}.\end{aligned}
$$

The function has critical points when $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}=0.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =0 \\ 4u{e}^{w} & =0 \\ u & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

The equation $u=0$ defines the plane $u=0,$ i.e., $vw$-plane.

Find the locations of all of the critical points of the transformation T, where T is defined as

T:[uvw]⟶[u2−vu2+vew].

a
The critical points lie on the plane w=u.
b
The critical points lie on the parabolic cylinder w2=2u.
c
The critical points lie on the sphere u2+v2+w2=1.
d
The critical points lie on the uv−plane.
e
The critical points lie on the vw−plane.
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

For a transformation

T:[uvw]→[x(u,v,w)y(u,v,w)z(u,v,w)],

the Jacobian determinant of T, denoted ∂(x,y,z)∂(u,v,w), is given by

∂(x,y,z)∂(u,v,w)=|∂x∂u∂x∂v∂x∂w∂y∂u∂y∂v∂y∂w∂z∂u∂z∂v∂z∂w|.

Here, we have

x(u,v,w)=u2−v,y(u,v,w)=u2+v,z(u,v,w)=ew.

First, we find the partial derivatives:

∂x∂u=2u∂x∂v=−1∂x∂w=0∂y∂u=2u∂y∂v=1∂y∂w=0∂z∂u=0∂z∂v=0∂z∂w=ew

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

∂(x,y,z)∂(u,v,w)=|2u−102u1000ew|=ew|2u−12u1|=ew(2u+2u)=4uew.

The function has critical points when ∂(x,y,z)∂(u,v,w)=0. So, we obtain

∂(x,y,z)∂(u,v,w)=04uew=0u=0.

The equation u=0 defines the plane u=0, i.e., vw-plane.

verification.explanation: Rechecking confirms det(DT)=e^w(2u·1−(−1)·2u)=4ue^w. Since e^w>0, the critical points are exactly u=0, the vw-plane, matching the worked solution. The displayed incorrect submission selected d, not e.

decision.explanation: The Jacobian matrix of (u,v,w) with respect to (x,y,z) is [[0,-1,1],[1,0,1],[-3,0,0]], whose determinant is 3. The requested transformation is the inverse, so its Jacobian determinant is 1/3.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation $T:(u,v,w)\to (x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w)),$ given that 

$$
u=z-y,\,v=x+z,\,w=-3x.
$$
after.worked_solution:
For a transformation 

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{aligned}],
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & \frac{∂x}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & \frac{∂y}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & \frac{∂z}{∂w}\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, we're only given ${T}^{-1}.$ So, we compute the Jacobian determinant of $T$ as follows:

- First, we compute $\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)},$ the Jacobian determinant of ${T}^{-1}.$

- Then, we will compute the Jacobian determinant of $T$ using the relation

$$
\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1}.
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & =0 & \,\frac{∂u}{∂y} & =-1 & \,\frac{∂u}{∂z} & =1 \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & =1 & \,\frac{∂v}{∂y} & =0 & \,\frac{∂v}{∂z} & =1 \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & =-3 & \,\frac{∂w}{∂y} & =0 & \,\frac{∂w}{∂z} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant of ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} & \frac{∂u}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y} & \frac{∂v}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & \frac{∂w}{∂y} & \frac{∂w}{∂z}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ -3 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =-(-1)|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -3 & 0\end{aligned}|+1|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -3 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =1(0+3)+1(0-0) \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we take the reciprocal:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & ={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation $T:(u,v,w)\to (x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w)),$ given that 

$$
u=z-y,\,v=x+z,\,w=-3x.
$$
content.worked_solution:
For a transformation 

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{aligned}],
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & \frac{∂x}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & \frac{∂y}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & \frac{∂z}{∂w}\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, we're only given ${T}^{-1}.$ So, we compute the Jacobian determinant of $T$ as follows:

- First, we compute $\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)},$ the Jacobian determinant of ${T}^{-1}.$

- Then, we will compute the Jacobian determinant of $T$ using the relation

$$
\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1}.
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & =0 & \,\frac{∂u}{∂y} & =-1 & \,\frac{∂u}{∂z} & =1 \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & =1 & \,\frac{∂v}{∂y} & =0 & \,\frac{∂v}{∂z} & =1 \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & =-3 & \,\frac{∂w}{∂y} & =0 & \,\frac{∂w}{∂z} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant of ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} & \frac{∂u}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y} & \frac{∂v}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & \frac{∂w}{∂y} & \frac{∂w}{∂z}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ -3 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =-(-1)|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -3 & 0\end{aligned}|+1|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -3 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =1(0+3)+1(0-0) \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we take the reciprocal:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & ={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
